Bill.BriefDescription: Regarding the humane treatment of dogs.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the humane treatment of dogs; adding a newsection to chapter 16.52 RCW; prescribing penalties; and providing aneffective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 16.52 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1)(a) It is unlawful to leave a dog outside and unattended by useof a restraint such as a tether, chain, rope, cord, or other deviceused to tie an animal to a running cable or pulley system or to astationary object under any of the following circumstances: (i) For more than one hour each day unless the owner or custodianis in the company of the animal or for no longer than is necessary forthe owner or custodian to complete a temporary task that requires thedog to be restrained and then for not more than three hours each day; (ii) During any declared weather advisories, warnings, oremergencies; (iii) In a manner that prevents the animal from lying, sitting, orstanding comfortably and without the restraint becoming taut; p. 1 HB 2387 (iv) In a manner that allows the animal to become entangled on therestraint or another object; (v) In a manner that restricts the animal's access to adequateshelter in temperatures that fall below forty degrees or above eightyfive degrees or during rain, hail, sleet, or snow; (vi) In a manner that restricts the animal's access to adequatefood and water; (vii) In a manner that leaves the animal in unsafe or unsanitaryconditions; (viii) In a manner that causes injury to the animal; (ix) In a location that is within one hundred yards of a school; or (x) In a manner that gives the animal access to any public rightofway, including through a fence. (b) Any tether, fastener, chain, tie, or other restraintpermissible under this section must be attached to a properly fittedharness or collar and provide enough room between the collar and thedog's throat through which two fingers may fit. Choke, pinch, or prongtype collars may not be used in tethering, fastening, chaining, tying,or otherwise restraining a dog. (c) Nothing in this section prevents: (i) The tethering, fastening, chaining, tying, or otherwiserestraining of a dog pursuant to the requirements of a camping orrecreational area; or (ii) The tethering, fastening, chaining, tying, or otherwiserestraining of a dog while engaged in, or actively training for, anactivity related to use of the dog as a service dog or by any militaryor law enforcement agency. (2) A dog owner who keeps the owner's dog in an enclosure for themajority of the day must comply with the housing facility and enclosurerequirements of section 2(2), chapter . . . (section 2(2) of EngrossedSubstitute Senate Bill No. 5651), Laws of 2009. (3) Each violation of this section is a separate offense. A personwho violates this section is subject to the following civil penalties: (a) For a first violation, a civil penalty of one hundred dollars; (b) For a second violation, a civil penalty of two hundred fiftydollars; and (c) For a third or subsequent violation, a civil penalty of five HB 2387 p. 2 hundred dollars.
